answer: Uniqueness is tested where faking is cheap and hiding is costly: a public beacon names one seat per horizon to solve an exclusive escrowed puzzle, and any second seat filing the same solution voids both bonds. Clones sharing a key or a cached answer collide at the first draw they win, so a farm of k can stay undetected only by holding k genuinely separate solving paths, and every pair among them becomes a forbidden equality, roughly k-squared constraints to maintain. The tundra of registered seats stays honest because a glacier of pooled secrets melts the moment two claimants collide.
